answers.charter-meetings: The ethics and compliance committee **shall meet at least four times per year** [1]. It **shall also meet at least annually with the audit committee** [1] to review major non-financial compliance matters [2].
answers.charter-min-directors: The ethics and compliance committee must consist of **no fewer than three non-employee directors**, each of whom must meet the New York Stock Exchange standards for director independence [1].
answers.charter-term-length: Ethics and compliance committee members are appointed by the board for **one-year terms**, on the recommendation of the directors and corporate governance committee. They serve such terms as the board may determine, or until their earlier removal, resignation, or death [1].
answers.charter-financial-oversight: The **audit committee** has sole oversight over matters of financial compliance, including accounting, auditing, financial reporting, and related investor disclosures [1]. The ethics and compliance committee has primary oversight of all other areas ("non-financial compliance"), and the two committees meet jointly at least annually to review major non-financial compliance matters [1].
answers.charter-section-name: According to the Composition and Term section, the chair of the ethics and compliance committee is designated by the board.
answers.redbook-report-concern: Under the Red Book, anyone, whether working for Lilly or not, can submit concerns about possible violations of laws and regulations, the Red Book, or company policies or procedures at https://speakup.lilly.com. Under the Supplier Code of Business Conduct, known or suspected violations can be reported to Lilly sponsors or the Lilly Ethics & Compliance Hotline (www.lillyethics.ethicspoint.com, or call 1-800-815-2481).
answers.redbook-values: Lilly's values are **Integrity, Excellence, and Respect for People** [1][3]. Lilly expects its suppliers and employees to conduct Lilly business consistent with high standards of corporate conduct and these values [1][3].
answers.redbook-last-step: The last step of the decision tree is **Step 5: Reflect and Learn**. It asks what went well, what could be improved, and whether there are lessons to share with your team.
answers.redbook-ai-bias: The Red Book says Lilly strives to mitigate any inherent bias or discrimination in data, information, or algorithms when using Artificial Intelligence (AI). This is part of its commitment to responsible AI use, which also includes protecting against unintended applications, unintended access, and harm, and promoting transparency in the use of AI.
answers.redbook-investigations: Yes. Investigation details, including discipline, are treated as confidential [1].
answers.supplier-excluded-employee: Under the Lilly Supplier Code of Business Conduct, a supplier must **report to Lilly within five (5) calendar days** if one of its employees is excluded or restricted in any way from doing business with any government.
answers.supplier-death-report: Under the Lilly Supplier Code of Business Conduct, any known or suspected death or suspect product must be reported **immediately (within 24 hours of receipt)** [1][2]. In the US, this is done by calling The Lilly Answers Center (TLAC) at 1.800.LillyRx (1.800.545.5979) or by using an alternative reporting method as determined by the Lilly component [1][2].
answers.supplier-hotline-number: The Lilly Ethics & Compliance Hotline phone number is **1-800-815-2481**. The hotline is also reachable online at www.lillyethics.ethicspoint.com.
answers.supplier-cooperative-learning: Under the Lilly Supplier Code of Business Conduct, "We do not use child labor (except as consistent with applicable law, such as cooperative learning programs)" [1][2]. Cooperative learning programs are given as an example of an exception to the child labor prohibition that is permitted when consistent with applicable law.
answers.supplier-impaired: No. Under the Lilly Supplier Code of Business Conduct, "we ensure that we are not impaired with drugs or alcohol while at work so that we can be fully engaged and help make life better for people around the world" [1][3].
answers.charter-statutes-reworded: The **ethics and compliance committee** does this. Under its charter, it reviews and identifies legal and regulatory trends and issues that may affect the company's business operations, financial performance, or reputation. When appropriate, it brings them to the attention of the board of directors [1].
answers.charter-statutes-typo: The **ethics and compliance committee** is responsible. Under its charter, the committee "shall review, identify, and when appropriate bring to the attention of the board of directors legal and regulatory trends and issues" that may affect the company's "business operations, financial performance or reputation" [1].
answers.supplier-adverse-event: Any other adverse event or product complaint must be reported within one business day, and any known or suspected death or suspect product must be reported immediately (within 24 hours of receipt). Outside the US, select your location from the globe link in the upper right corner of Lilly.com, then click "Contact" or "Contact Us" in the top menu bar to access the appropriate local reporting method.
answers.retaliation: No. Lilly does not tolerate retaliation for reporting inappropriate conduct, preventing unlawful practices, or participating in an investigation, and it takes appropriate measures to prevent retaliation against people who make reports [1][2]. Employees may share concerns openly and honestly, even anonymously, knowing that Lilly will not tolerate acts of retaliation [3]. Retaliation is also listed as inappropriate conduct that Lilly does not tolerate [4].
answers.supplier-purchasing: Under excerpt [2], purchasing goods or services requires **authorization from procurement, assessment by third party risk management, and appropriate supporting contractual documentation**. Excerpt [1], which appears to be a different version of the same section, lists only **authorization from procurement and appropriate supporting documentation**. Both versions also require having appropriate authority and securing the required Lilly approvals before acquiring or committing Lilly resources or disbursing Lilly funds.
answers.supplier-gifts-on-behalf: Suppliers may not offer gifts or donations on Lilly's behalf **without prior written approval** [1][2]. Separately, Lilly does not accept gifts, entertainment, or favors from suppliers that could affect or appear to affect its business judgment [1][2].
answers.supplier-current-version: The most recent version in the provided excerpts is **V15.0 (©2025)** of the Lilly Supplier Code of Business Conduct [2]. The excerpts also include an earlier Version 13.0 (©2021) [1].
answers.vacation-days: This is not covered in the provided policy documents.
